session_summary: Debugged training hang in Transformer AnswerVerifier (bert-base-uncased). The model loaded successfully but training appeared stuck after the LOAD REPORT and parameter count printout.

files_modified.change: Moved tokenization from __getitem__ (on-the-fly, one sample at a time) to __init__ (batched, single call). Removed per-sample tokenizer calls with padding='max_length'=384.
files_modified.rationale: On-the-fly tokenization with num_workers=0 caused sequential per-sample tokenization of 384 tokens for 948,716 training samples — extremely slow before the first batch appeared. Batched tokenization is much faster and __getitem__ now just indexes pre-computed tensors.

root_cause.symptom: Training hung after 'BertForSequenceClassification LOAD REPORT' and 'trainable params: 294,912 || all params: 109,778,690 || trainable%: 0.2686'
root_cause.cause: TextDataset.__getitem__ called tokenizer individually for each sample with padding='max_length'=384. With num_workers=0 in DataLoader, the first batch required 16 sequential tokenizations of 384-token sequences before any tqdm output appeared.
root_cause.fix: Pre-tokenize all texts in __init__ tokenizer(texts, ...) which uses HuggingFace's fast batched Rust tokenizer. __getitem__ now returns pre-computed tensors via indexing.

architecture_notes.data: 279,035 rows (train=237,179 val=41,856) → 948,716 training examples after prepare_answer_verifier_data (4 per MCQ row)
architecture_notes.training_config: epochs=5, batch_size=16, lr=2e-5, max_length=384, patience=2, AdamW + CosineAnnealingLR + AMP

misc_tips: Suppress HF logging noise with: transformers.logging.set_verbosity_error() before training
UNEXPECTED keys in LOAD REPORT (cls.predictions.*, cls.seq_relationship.*) are from BERT pre-training head — safe to ignore when loading for classification
MISSING keys (classifier.weight, classifier.bias) are the newly initialized classification head — expected
